audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was given to Irelia while the page's own whys[0] says 'step into the wave and lay Poison Trail so she pays a tax for every last-hit', and Level 3 was given to Singed while whys[2] says the level-3 stun-into-all-in is 'her edge'. Both rows contradicted the sentence printed beside them.
audit.why: The packet chart (Singed, Skill, Irelia, Singed, Irelia, Singed, Singed) matches the prose exactly and matches the 55.82% Emerald+ win rate over 1023 games.
audit.corrected: Level 1 to Singed and Level 3 to Irelia, flipped as one atomic group across both layers; the two phase whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty 7.5/10 and 'Tricky' on a 55.82% favoured matchup, and no phase named a real spike — Vanguard's Edge had no cooldown attached anywhere.
audit.why: Her spikes are Flawless Duet at 3, Vanguard's Edge at 6 (125/105/85), and her first item; yours are Rylai's and the two-item window.
audit.corrected: diffRating 4/10, diff FAV, difficulty and final-rating rows matched; Vanguard's Edge given its 125s cooldown and Ionian Fervor named instead of 'stacked passive'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states the exact opposite of the truth on the matchup's decisive interaction. wants.foe[2] tells the reader Irelia can 'negate your Mega Adhesive root by simply dashing over it'. She cannot: Mega Adhesive grounds, Bladesurge is a dash, and Irelia's own kit file flags it 'mobility that grounding and walls can deny' — inside the glue Bladesurge will not cast at all. Separately, Defiant Dance is credited with healing in four places ('her W heal', 'her W burst-heal', 'melts her W healing', 'it will heal her for a chunk'). Defiant Dance does not heal; Riot's text is 'charges a strike that deals more damage as she charges. She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' The healing is on Bladesurge. And that damage reduction is PHYSICAL only, so Poison Trail's magic damage passes through the charge untouched — a free fact the page never had.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon descriptions for Irelia Q/W and Singed W.
audit.corrected: Grounding stated as the reason Bladesurge cannot escape the glue; healing re-attributed from Defiant Dance to Bladesurge everywhere; Defiant Dance's physical-only damage reduction written in as a reason to keep running poison through it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' for this matchup, and it was right — not one number appeared on either layer.
audit.why: Bladesurge is 10/9/8/7/6 at 600 range and refreshes on a Marked target or a kill; Defiant Dance 20/18/16/14/12; Flawless Duet 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 at 850; Vanguard's Edge 125/105/85. Singed's Mega Adhesive is 17/16/15/14/13 and Fling 10/9.5/9/8.5/8.
audit.corrected: Concrete 'step up only after Flawless Duet is spent' sequencing added to the Levels 4-5 phase, the cooldown block and the tracked-ability do, with real rank-1 numbers.

audit.why: Flawless Duet carries a derived 'grounding' flag, but Riot's description is only 'damaged, stunned and Marked' — no grounding. Left unwritten. Vanguard's Edge's terrain flag IS supported ('the blades form a wall that will damage and slow enemies that walk through it') and the page already describes it correctly as walling you in.

edits.before: At levels 1 through 2 Irelia cannot Q to you — she can only Q to minions — so step into her wave and drop Poison Trail through it. She will either eat ticking damage to last-hit or back off. Do not give her passive stacks for free by standing still; move laterally so she must walk through the cloud to auto you. If she over-commits before her passive is stacked, Fling her into your minions; the landing puts her in poison and denies the mark she needed for her W heal. She hits level 2 and starts fishing for her E stun, so watch her foot position relative to any narrow brush entrance — that is her setup angle.

edits.before: Level 6 with Vanguard's Edge is her power peak: fully stacked passive, shred, a line skillshot that walls you in for the all-in. Pop Insanity Potion the moment she marks you with E so the armor and MR absorb the burst while you run through Mega Adhesive and out the back. Do not try to Fling her mid-combo when she has W active — it will heal her for a chunk. Instead proxy the wave under her tower during her passive-stack downtime at levels 4 and 5; she cannot Q-dash to you through an empty lane, and every minion wave she loses is damage you did without fighting. At 6 stay in open terrain where running past her is viable — never fight her in the pixel-wide jungle entrance.

Defiant Dance only reduces physical damage, so Poison Trail burns straight through the charge. Instead proxy the wave under her tower during her passive-stack downtime at levels 4 and 5; she cannot Q-dash to you through an empty lane, and every minion wave she loses is damage you did without fighting. edits.before: Rylai's is the matchup-defining item. Once it completes, every Fling drops her into a slowed Poison Trail she cannot Q-dash away from, and her W burst-heal cannot keep pace with Liandry's stacking burn over the next four seconds. Force side-lane skirmishes, not teamfights where she can Q-reset freely through five targets. If she builds Sterak's or Unflinching, your W adhesive still roots her on exit — root into Fling into run-past is your closer all game. She needs your team to be occupied to splitpush against you; set up the wave to bounce toward your tower and proxy behind hers, making her choose between defending base and chasing a Singed she cannot catch.

notes: The worst error on this page told the player the opposite of the truth: wants.foe[2] said Irelia could 'negate your Mega Adhesive root by simply dashing over it'. Mega Adhesive grounds and Bladesurge is a dash — her own kit file flags it as deniable by grounding. A Singed reading that line would stop using his best tool against her. Second: Defiant Dance was credited with healing in four separate places; it has no heal at all (the heal is on Bladesurge), and its damage reduction is physical-only, so Poison Trail passes straight through it. Flawless Duet's derived 'grounding' flag is a false positive (Riot text: damaged, stunned and Marked) and was not written. Chart flipped in two rows to match the page's own whys and the packet.
